newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower as May leads losers.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower as May leads losers.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended sharply lower, with nearby May hit hard by fund long liquidation, traders said.

"It appears to be position-rolling and liquidating May longs via the (July/May) bear spread," a trader said. "I think it's technically-related. Most of it appears to be funds rolling their positions. Benson-Quinn has been the leader, bear-spreading at least four million July/May."
Traders said the May/July spread oscillated throughout the day. It traded as wide as 16 cents per bushel late but narrowed from that level to close at eight cents.

KCBT wheat saw early weakness after needed rains fell over the weekend in Europe and in parts of the U.S. Plains, traders said. U.S. meteorology firm Weather Services Corp said western Europe received light to moderate rain, but that conditions would likely stay dry for much of the coming week.
KCBT wheat settled five to 21 cents per bushel lower, with May down 21 cents at $4.49. July lost 12 cents to close at $4.41.

Other large players besides Benson-Quinn included E D & F Man International, which bull-spread one million May/July at 11 to 15 cents. Refco sold 3.4 million July and Linnco sold 1.5 million July. Cargill Investor Services bought 1.8 million May and 1.4 million July.
